tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(seed): reject multi-document YAML and verify a merge before trusting it

CRITICAL data-loss bug, found live via a reviewer repro before it shipped:
additiveMerge treated a front-matter Markdown file ("---\n...\n---\n" then
a body) as if its front matter described the WHOLE file. yaml.Unmarshal
silently decodes only the first of the two YAML documents that front
matter actually is, so topLevelMapping saw a normal-looking mapping — but
keyBlocks' "end of file for the last key" is wrong once a second document
follows: the last front-matter key's "block" swallowed the closing "---",
the heading, and the entire body. additiveMerge appended that whole
swallowed tail onto a user's own customized agent/skill .md.

Two independent fixes, per the reviewer's recommendation:

1. topLevelMapping now requires exactly one YAML document (yaml.NewDecoder,
   reject if a second Decode succeeds) — closes the front-matter case
   directly, at the source of the wrong assumption.

2. additiveMerge re-decodes its own assembled result and requires it
   DeepEqual the shipped content's decoded value before returning ok=true.
   This is independent defense, not redundant with (1): a flow-style
   mapping ("{a: 1, b: 2}") puts every key on the same line, so keyBlocks'
   line ranges do not separate them at all, and the result silently drops
   a key on decode rather than erroring — a case (1) does not touch. Post-
   merge verification catches it because a dropped or altered key fails
   DeepEqual against what the shipped content actually defines.

Tests: front-matter Markdown declines (the exact repro shape), a flow-style
mapping declines, and post-merge verification is exercised directly as the
safety net that catches a bad merge independent of any specific line-
slicing bug.
EOF
)"
